comparator.sourceNotes: The formally adopted 2026-2027 regulations define a 180-ECTS Theology bachelor and four variants: with or without Greek, each with or without the PThU trajectory. The PThU trajectory with Greek is selected under the broad-academic-identity rule because it combines both biblical source languages with biblical, systematic, historical, intercultural and practical theology, and the current public programme page identifies it as the most commonly chosen variant. In Year 2 the PThU rules replace the ordinary media/text choice with Psychology and Sociology of Religion and replace Religion and Politics with Dogmatics. Year 3 is the prescribed 30-ECTS PThU block plus a specialization, Thesis Seminar, Science Communication and thesis. Origins of Religion: Foundational Texts and their Transformations is selected as the first specialization in official order, independently of UCR fit. The live programme page, current study-guide index and adopted regulations were rechecked on 2026-10-14; the settled route and curriculum remain unchanged. alternatives.concept: Study questions of belief, meaning and the good life through philosophy, myth, literature, history, archaeology and visual heritage, then examine religious traditions' cultural and political contexts through sociology, psychology, law and politics. This is a related-fields programme, not a substitute for Christian theology, biblical languages, exegesis or pastoral formation.

alternatives.concept: Combine moral philosophy and human-rights reasoning with explicit AI ethics, biomedical and genetic foundations, human physiology and disease, sustainability governance, circular economy and renewable-system design. This responds to target-linked ethical questions about technology, genetic intervention, human life and climate through related disciplines rather than theological ethics.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Twenty courses, or 150 EC, differ in each direction. The first programme's history, literature, heritage, public-life and religion-adjacent social analysis are replaced by explicit AI ethics, molecular and physiological science, genetics and disease, sustainability governance, circular economy and renewable-system study. These changes are direct curricular consequences of the separate contemporary-ethics evidence, not threshold-filling substitutions.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The historical judgment correctly identified the absence of disciplinary theology, biblical languages and pastoral formation but applied a full-substitution threshold. One complete related-fields programme is defensible in belief, cultural traditions and public life, and the separately evidenced contemporary-ethics cluster supports a second complete and materially distinct programme. The next candidate—biblical languages, exegesis and confessional theology—is not feasible, so production stops at two. Ministry, spiritual care and religious education were also assessed and remain infeasible for missing religion-specific academic and practice formation.

notes.text: The Groningen programme is a Theology degree built around Hebrew and Greek, biblical texts and exegesis, Christian thought, dogmatics, practical, historical, biblical, intercultural and ethical theology, and a Theology thesis. UCR can study belief, meaning, cultural traditions, public life and contemporary ethical questions through adjacent humanities, social sciences, biomedicine and sustainability, but neither UCR route reproduces the theological discipline.

UCR offers no biblical Hebrew or Greek, sustained scriptural exegesis, dogmatics, systematic or practical theology, pastoral formation, ministry preparation or supervised spiritual-care practice. The included programmes therefore remain bounded related-field responses.
